name: Paul Volcker
role: Chair of the US Federal Reserve (1979–1987) and financial-reform advocate
summary: Volcker prioritized price stability, an independent central bank and effective public administration. He defended a regulated private financial system, broader healthcare provision and market-based climate action, and warned late in life against plutocracy and attacks on democratic institutions.

universal-healthcare.rationale: He explicitly supports more universal healthcare and the government intervention needed to provide it.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He endorses free enterprise and criticizes government management of economic activities it performed poorly.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He demands binding restrictions on bank risk-taking and stronger supervision of systemic financial institutions.

state-harmful.rationale: He insists government is indispensable and should earn democratic trust through competent administration.

limit-growth.rationale: His climate proposal explicitly seeks emissions cuts while promoting economic growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He signed a call for immediate national action and an annually rising carbon tax until emissions goals are achieved.

central-planning.rationale: He credits the retreat from extensive government economic control while retaining an important regulatory role.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: He defends the Federal Reserve’s continuing independent monetary and supervisory functions.

democracy-best.rationale: His final writings seek to preserve democratic institutions and restore confidence in democratic government.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: He criticizes large deficits and says tax cuts should be matched by spending reductions.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: His escalating carbon-price proposal steers investment and consumption away from high-emission energy.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He identifies public health, social security, healthcare and environmental protection as essential government responsibilities.

separated-powers.rationale: His final afterword explicitly defends separation of powers as a democratic pillar.

party-controls-media.rationale: His final warning treats attacks on an independent free press as attacks on democracy.

central-bank-independence.rationale: His mature position combines central-bank independence with a primary commitment to stable prices.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He identifies the rule of law as an essential protection against threats to American democracy.

no-bailouts.rationale: He justifies emergency rescues during systemic collapse but wants future failing investment institutions liquidated with owners and creditors exposed.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: His reforms aim to restore a functioning private financial system after crisis rather than replace it.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: He urges attention to public administration and active commitment to democratic governance.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He warns that extreme wealth is turning the country into a plutocracy and reshaping political power.

pollution-taxes.rationale: His signed statement favors carbon pricing over less efficient regulatory controls.

no-business-privileges.rationale: He objects to the funding advantage and excessive risk-taking created by expected government rescues of giant financial firms.

notes: Whole-career review covers Treasury monetary work, 1971 suspension of gold convertibility, the inflation shock and associated recession, financial crises, 2000 policy retrospective, post-2008 reforms, 2018 memoir and 2019 final statements. Downloaded and searched the full Federal Reserve oral history and 2010 reform article. Reviewed all 490 statements and remaining nulls against the evidence across all ten themes. PATCO: he described weakened labor bargaining as helping disinflation; that is not a stated general prohibition on unions or a particular strike-restriction law, so those propositions remain unknown. Carbon dividends are not an unconditional basic-income program. Fiscal prudence is not evidence for a binding legal borrowing rule. Currency stability is not automatically a general common-currency endorsement. Most family, religious, penal, military-intervention and digital-rights questions remain undocumented. No inferred answers.
